overview: The Historical Commission considered demolition delay applications and determinations of significance for several residential properties across the city. The commission also met with Medford's new building commissioner to discuss coordination on demolition reviews and reviewed ongoing historical projects.

items.title: 27 Allmont Street: Determination of Significance
items.summary: The commission determined 27 Allmont Street to be historically significant due to its Greek Revival architecture and association with the local shipbuilding industry, advancing it to a preferably preserved hearing.

items.title: 82 Greenleaf Avenue: Demolition Application and Determination of Significance
items.summary: The commission accepted the demolition application but voted that the property was not historically significant following extensive fire damage and prior alterations.

items.title: 289 Fells Way West: Demolition Application
items.summary: The commission accepted the demolition application and voted to pass on further historic review because the structure had already largely collapsed.

items.title: Demolition Applications: 18 Wedgmere Road and 9 Trout Avenue
items.summary: Accepted partial demolition applications for roof alterations at 18 Wedgmere Road and 9 Trout Avenue, scheduling significance hearings for the following month.

items.title: Discussion with Building Commissioner Scott Vandewalle
items.summary: Building Commissioner Scott Vandewalle introduced himself to discuss streamlining permitting, handling damaged properties, and coordinating historical reviews with the commission.

items.title: Commission Project Updates
items.summary: Ryan Hayward updated the board on bidding requirements for the Cross Street cemetery archaeological excavation, Community Preservation Act funding for Thomas Brooks Park, survey work in Fulton Heights, and historical interpretive signage at Riverbend Park.

items.title: Approval of Minutes
items.summary: Approved the meeting minutes from March 2024.
